definitions.explanation: Shifting an entire piece of music or passage to a different key while preserving the intervals between notes. A fundamental concept in music theory and performance.

examples.japanese: ⟦{曲|きょく}→曲：09881_kyoku⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{移調|いちょう}⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: To transpose a piece of music.

examples.japanese: ⟦{歌|うた}い→歌う：00684_utau⟧やすいよう⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{半音|はんおん}⟦{下|さ}げて→下げる：00807_sageru⟧{移調|いちょう}⟦した→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: I transposed it down a half step to make it easier to sing.

examples.japanese: ⟦クラリネット→クラリネット：08138_kurarinetto⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{移調|いちょう}⟦{楽器|がっき}→楽器：13159_gakki⟧な⟦の→の：09472_no⟧で、{実音|じつおん}⟦と→と：00512_to⟧{記譜|きふ}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{異|こと}なる→異なる：02101_kotonaru⟧。
examples.english: The clarinet is a transposing instrument, so the actual pitch differs from the written notation.

notes:
{移調|いちょう} is a music theory term meaning to shift a piece of music to a different key while keeping all the intervals between notes the same.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {移調|いちょう}⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: to transpose
- {移調|いちょう}⟦{楽器|がっき}→楽器：13159_gakki⟧: transposing instrument (e.g., clarinet, trumpet — instruments whose written notes differ from their sounding pitch)
- {半音|はんおん}⟦{上|あ}げて→上げる：02443_ageru⟧{移調|いちょう}⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: transpose up a half step
- {半音|はんおん}⟦{下|さ}げて→下げる：00807_sageru⟧{移調|いちょう}⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: transpose down a half step

WATCH OUT:
Several common words share the reading いちょう:
- ⟦{胃腸|いちょう}→胃腸：15503_ichou⟧: stomach and intestines
- ⟦{銀杏|いちょう}→銀杏：04379_ichou⟧: ginkgo tree
- ⟦{市長|しちょう}→市長：12472_shichou⟧: mayor (different reading but sometimes confused)
